name: bada-cinevim
description: Bada CineVim — a cinematic VIM editor for the Bada quantum programming language. Whatever the pointer or the cursor is on is blown up in place — no magnifying glass needed — moving up or down lifts that whole row, and moving right or left makes the pointed spot within it larger still. Each line is cut into word-sized segments and scaled by a two-axis fisheye: vertically by distance in rows and horizontally by distance in pixels, combined as 1 + (zpeak-1)·gv·(vmix + (1-vmix)·gh) — not a plain product, so a share (vmix) of the vertical lift applies across the whole row. Distances are always measured in unmagnified coordinates, and the pointer is mapped back from display space to natural space, so the magnification never shoves its own focus around. The extra width and height are redistributed by offsets[i] = sum_{j<i} size_j(k_j-1) + size_i(k_i-1)·anchor (centre anchor vertically, start anchor horizontally), so characters never overlap at any zoom, and since no margins move there is no per-frame relayout. Underneath it is still a line buffer, so every VIM motion and operator keeps working, and Japanese IME input is supported. Also includes a depth-of-field code view, an event-processing flash effect driven by an event bus, an Academy-leader movie countdown and a quantum Bada runtime (qubit / H / CNOT / measure). Self-contained HTML app, zero dependencies, fully offline.
author: Masaaki Yamaguchi
